name: MissionDecision has no firefighter channel — every field is UAV-keyed
evidence: The full field list is: `uav_assignments: dict[str, str]`, `task_assignments: dict[str, str]`, `mission_mode: str`, `relay_assignments: dict[str, str]`, `recall_orders: tuple[str, ...]`, plus confidence/uncertainty/comparison/explanation/selected_option_id/notes. There is no firefighter_assignments, no defend_region, no sector, no firefighter_id. The global layer's output type literally has nowhere to put a firefighter order, so the break is upstream of any plumbing question — even a perfectly wired executor would have nothing to read. This is the root break: it is why the background arming experiment that populated `uav_assignments` as a proper dict changed outcomes while the fire map stayed byte-identical — the only thing a MissionDecision can move is UAVs.
